messages.content: Who is Aaron?

Aaron Rohrbacher is a Technical Lead and Senior Software Engineer specializing in full-stack and DevOps. He is based in Portland, Oregon, and currently works remotely as Lead Software Development Engineer at Forbes AAC.
What does Aaron do?

Aaron is a language-agnostic senior software engineer with deep expertise across the full stack, DevOps, AI/ML, and cloud architecture on AWS, GCP, and Azure. He leads engineering teams and has delivered production systems in assistive technology, finance, HR, payroll, and logistics.
Tell me about Aaron.

Aaron Rohrbacher is a Technical Lead and Senior Software Engineer based in Portland, Oregon. He builds high-performing teams and delivers resilient cloud-native systems, currently as Lead Software Development Engineer at Forbes AAC.
Give me an overview of Aaron.

Aaron is a senior full-stack and DevOps engineer with language-agnostic expertise and deep vertical experience in assistive tech, finance, HR, payroll, and logistics. He has owned multiple environments from 0-to-1 through long-term maintenance across AWS, GCP, and Azure.

What is Forbes AAC?

Forbes AAC is an assistive technology company building software for Augmentative and Alternative Communication — tools that help people with speech and language disabilities communicate. Aaron joined in August 2025 as Lead Software Development Engineer.
What does Aaron do at Forbes AAC?

Aaron leads stabilization of a mission-critical assistive technology platform and architected an enterprise-grade replacement with his team. He rebuilt the native apps across iOS in Swift, Android in Java/Kotlin, macOS in Swift, and Windows/Linux in Qt and Rust.
Tell me about Aaron's work at Forbes AAC.

Aaron built and led a team from scratch to rescue a failing Ruby 2.6 and Ember 3.0 platform, stabilizing it in days rather than months and preventing data loss. He then architected and delivered a Next.js-based enterprise rebuild alongside native apps for iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, and Linux.
What did Aaron rescue at Forbes AAC?

Aaron rescued a mission-critical assistive technology platform on the verge of collapse, including an Android app about to be removed from Google Play and an iOS app crashing on current OS versions. He stabilized the entire system and brought all apps back into compliance.
What tech does Forbes AAC use?

Under Aaron's architecture, Forbes AAC's rebuilt stack uses Next.js with SSR for the main application, Swift and SwiftUI for iOS, Java and Kotlin for Android, Swift with AppKit for macOS, and Qt on Rust for Windows and Linux. The legacy system was Ruby 2.6 and Ember 3.0 on Heroku.
What does AAC stand for?

AAC stands for Augmentative and Alternative Communication — technology that helps people with speech and language disabilities communicate. Aaron has worked in the AAC vertical at both Forbes AAC and through SPARQ.
How did Aaron handle the Heroku shutdown?

Aaron negotiated directly with Heroku to prevent platform shutdown, then executed an emergency infrastructure upgrade under extreme time pressure while keeping all stakeholders informed. This preserved service for users who depend on the platform for daily communication.
What was the Ember migration at Forbes AAC?

Aaron led an incremental Ruby upgrade and built custom tooling to convert deprecated Ember 3.0 code into maintainable JavaScript, preserving years of clinician-driven feature refinement. The migration path used Next.js with SSR to bridge the compiled legacy code.
What did Aaron do at SPARQ?

At SPARQ from August 2022 to February 2025, Aaron was Technical Lead and Senior Software Engineer, delivering architecture and implementation across enterprise consulting engagements in AAC, global logistics, and payroll. His AAC work led directly to being recruited by Forbes AAC.
Tell me about Aaron's work at SPARQ.

At SPARQ Aaron served as sole technical lead on multiple enterprise projects, designed microservices and APIs on AWS Lambda and Node.js, and led the phase-one production deployment of a payroll overhaul for a global logistics leader serving over 500,000 employees. He also mentored offshore teams on CI/CD, GCP, and cloud computing best practices.
What is SPARQ?
SPARQ is a technology consulting firm based in Atlanta, Georgia. Aaron worked there remotely as Technical Lead and Senior Software Engineer from August 2022 to February 2025.
What payroll work did Aaron do?

At SPARQ Aaron was impactful as a leader in the phase-one production deployment of a full payroll system overhaul for a global logistics leader, delivering a modern multi-system integration API that serves over 500,000 employees.
Has Aaron worked with offshore teams?

Yes — at SPARQ Aaron led offshore development teams on ADO CI/CD, GCP deployment, and dev environment standardization. He mentored those teams and stakeholder leadership on modern cloud computing practices.
What was Aaron's role at Nordic Semiconductor?

Aaron worked as a Software Engineer at Nordic Semiconductor in Portland, Oregon, from February to March 2022. He developed test automation tools for AWS in Node.js using React, Jest, Cypress, Linux, and Istanbul, and built Nordic's first 'thingy lab' for IoT experimentation.
What did Aaron build at Nordic?

Aaron built Nordic Semiconductor's first 'thingy lab' — a space where IoT device experiments on Nordic's proprietary dashboard platform could be combined flexibly without leaving the room. He also developed AWS test automation tooling in Node.js.
What is Nuel Cloud Computing?

Nuel Cloud Computing is a cloud hosting startup Aaron founded and ran from August 2020 to February 2024 in Portland, Oregon. He architected a proprietary AWS solution to provision containerized LAMP stacks for WordPress and PHP developers using ECS, EKS, Node.js, Express, Python, and the Serverless Framework.
Did Aaron run his own company?

Yes — Aaron founded and ran Nuel Cloud Computing from 2020 to 2024 as Proprietor, Systems Architect, and Engineering Manager. He built a self-service WordPress and PHP hosting platform with market-leading speeds at competitive prices.
What did Aaron build at Nuel?

At Nuel Cloud Computing Aaron built a self-service customer dashboard in React and Node.js for automated signup, legacy migration, stack customization, and plugin management. He also delivered optimized caching and CloudFront CDN integration for fast WordPress and PHP performance, and provided security and vulnerability assessments.
What did Aaron do at Fiduciary Benchmarks?

Aaron was a Junior Software Development Engineer at Fiduciary Benchmarks in Lake Oswego, Oregon, from July 2018 to August 2021. He designed and maintained automated test suites in Cypress with JavaScript, analyzed and debugged issues, and implemented the WalkMe digital adoption platform.
What was Aaron's first job in tech?

Aaron's first software role was as a Web Development Intern at Planet Argon in Portland, Oregon, in early 2018. He worked on client projects for NIKE, Aloha Foods, and PAC global, building test suite enhancements and Spree eCommerce integrations.
What is Planet Argon?
Planet Argon is a Portland-based web development agency where Aaron interned in January and February 2018. He worked on client projects including NIKE, Aloha Foods, and PAC global.
Has Aaron ever taught?
Yes — before his software engineering career, Aaron was Faculty and Instructor of Clarinet and Saxophone at Cascade School of Music in Bend, Oregon, from January 2007 to August 2017.
What programming languages does Aaron know?

Aaron is proficient in JavaScript and TypeScript, Python, Rust, Ruby, Java and Kotlin, Swift, Bash, PowerShell, PHP, and SQL. He also has experience with COBOL and mainframe queries, and considers himself language-agnostic.
What languages does Aaron code in?
Aaron codes in JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Rust, Ruby, Java, Kotlin, Swift, PHP, SQL, Bash, and PowerShell. He is language-agnostic and picks up new languages as production work requires.

Yes — Aaron uses Rust in production. At Forbes AAC he rebuilt the Windows and Linux desktop applications using Qt on Rust.

Yes — Python is one of Aaron's core languages. He uses it for AI and ML work with PyTorch, for backend services, and for personal projects like his video processing tool Thinger.

Yes — JavaScript and TypeScript are among Aaron's primary languages. He works extensively with Node.js, Next.js, React, Express, and other JS ecosystem tools in production.

Yes — Aaron uses Swift professionally for iOS and macOS development. At Forbes AAC he rebuilt the iOS app with Swift and SwiftUI and the macOS app with Swift and AppKit.

Yes — Aaron has extensive Ruby experience. He led a Ruby 2.6 stabilization and upgrade at Forbes AAC and has worked with Rails across multiple projects.

Yes — Aaron has experience with COBOL and mainframe queries, which is unusual for a modern full-stack engineer.

Aaron primarily uses Next.js and React, and has shipped production work with Vue.js, Angular, and Ember.js. He also uses Rails on the Ruby side and Express on Node.js.
Does Aaron use Next.js?
Yes — Next.js is one of Aaron's primary frameworks. He used it to architect the Forbes AAC enterprise rebuild and to build this portfolio site, deployed via SST to AWS.
What is SST?

SST — the Serverless Stack — is an infrastructure-as-code framework for deploying full-stack applications to AWS. Aaron uses SST to deploy this portfolio site as a Lambda function with all surrounding infrastructure.
What cloud platforms does Aaron work with?

Aaron works across AWS, GCP, and Azure. AWS is his deepest area, including Lambda, ECS/EKS, EC2, API Gateway, CloudFormation, VPC, Route53, IAM, Cognito, S3, CloudFront, RDS, DynamoDB, SES/SNS/SQS, and CloudWatch.
What AWS services does Aaron know?

Aaron has production experience with Lambda, ECS/EKS, EC2, API Gateway, CloudFormation, VPC, Route53, IAM, Cognito, S3, CloudFront, RDS, DynamoDB, SES, SNS, SQS, CloudWatch, Cost Management, and Systems Manager.
Does Aaron use Lambda?
Yes — AWS Lambda is one of Aaron's most-used services. At SPARQ he designed microservices and APIs on AWS Lambda and Node.js for enterprise clients.
Does Aaron use GCP?
Yes — Aaron works with GCP including Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, Compute Engine, Cloud SQL, and Pub/Sub. At SPARQ he modernized payroll integration APIs using GCP Cloud Run.
Does Aaron use Azure?
Yes — Aaron has experience with Azure and Azure DevOps, including equivalents to AWS services and the full ADO CI/CD pipeline.
What AI tools does Aaron use?
Aaron works with PyTorch for custom LLM implementation and fine-tuning, natural language processing, and conversational AI. He uses Amazon Lex, Polly, Transcribe, and Amazon Q for AWS-native AI.
Tell me about Aaron's AI experience.

Aaron has built and fine-tuned custom LLMs using PyTorch, delivered conversational AI experiences for enterprise clients, and worked with Amazon's AI stack including Lex, Polly, Transcribe, and Q. He also built a GPT-2 model fine-tuned on George Carlin transcripts as a personal project.

Yes — AI and machine learning are a core focus of Aaron's work. He uses PyTorch for custom LLM implementation, does NLP, and has delivered production conversational AI for enterprise clients.

PyTorch is an open-source machine learning framework Aaron uses for custom LLM implementation, model development, and fine-tuning. It is one of his primary AI and ML tools.
What is Amazon Lex?
Amazon Lex is an AWS service for building conversational interfaces. Aaron uses it alongside Polly, Transcribe, and Amazon Q for conversational AI experiences.

Aaron uses Docker, Kubernetes, ECS, EKS, Terraform, AWS CDK, CloudFormation, and SST for infrastructure as code. For CI/CD he works with GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps, and Jenkins.

Does Aaron use Terraform?
Yes — Terraform is part of Aaron's infrastructure-as-code toolkit alongside AWS CDK, CloudFormation, and SST. He is a strong advocate for IaC and zero-downtime deployments.
What CI/CD tools does Aaron use?
Aaron works with GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps, and Jenkins for CI/CD. He has led multiple teams in standardizing CI/CD practices.
What's Aaron's DevOps background?

Aaron is a DevOps Architect with deep experience in container orchestration, microservices, serverless architecture, and infrastructure as code. He works across AWS, GCP, and Azure and has mentored offshore teams on modern cloud practices.

Aaron works with PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB, MongoDB, DynamoDB, and Redis including ElastiCache. He has experience with database optimization, scaling, and data migration strategies.

Does Aaron know Redis?

Aaron builds native mobile apps on iOS using Swift with UIKit and SwiftUI, and on Android using Java and Kotlin. He has also worked with React Native and Cordova for cross-platform apps.

Yes — Aaron builds native iOS apps using Swift with UIKit and SwiftUI. At Forbes AAC he stabilized and rebuilt the iOS app for current iOS versions.

Yes — Aaron builds native Android apps using Java and Kotlin. At Forbes AAC he rescued the Android app from being removed from Google Play by bringing it into compliance with current store standards.

Does Aaron build desktop apps?
Yes — Aaron builds desktop apps across macOS using Swift and AppKit, and Windows and Linux using Qt on Rust. At Forbes AAC he delivered all of these platforms in native code.

Yes — Aaron has hands-on experience with penetration testing using Burp Suite, OWASP Top 10 vulnerability assessments, SOC 2 compliance preparation, and IAM and access control. At SPARQ he served on the security and risk management team for enterprise clients.
Has Aaron done penetration testing?
Yes — Aaron has performed penetration testing and vulnerability assessments using Burp Suite, targeting OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, both at SPARQ and at Nuel Cloud Computing.

Aaron delivers resilient, scalable systems across the full stack and DevOps, mentors engineers, and brings calm execution in crisis situations. His track record includes rescuing mission-critical platforms and shipping enterprise systems across AAC, payroll, and logistics.
